episodes.166485: Low pressure moved from New York City early in the morning to New Hampshire and Maine by late morning.  A cluster of heavy showers and thunderstorms moved across southeast MA just before daybreak.
episodes.168298: Heavy rain brought flooding to a couple of rivers in the early part of April.
episodes.168612: A slow moving frontal system produced widespread heavy rainfall and flooding across eastern New York from April 7-8, 2022. Rainfall amounts between 1.50 and 3.00 inches were common, though a few localized areas received upwards of 4.50 inches. Periods of light to moderate rainfall began during the daytime hours on April 7 with the steadiest and heaviest rainfall arriving during the evening hours on April 7 into the overnight hours on April 8 before ending.||This heavy rainfall led to over a dozen rivers to exceed minor flood stage with a few rivers reaching moderate flood stage. For some, it took days after the event for waters to recede. ||In addition to the heavy rainfall and widespread flooding, strong winds developed across portions of the Taconics with peak gusts in the 35-50 mph range.||The combination of rain and wind led to only sporadic power outages. As a result of the heavy rain and flooding, a Travel Advisory was issued for Montgomery County during the overnight hours of April 7.
episodes.168613: A slow moving frontal system produced heavy rainfall across southern Vermont from April 7-8, 2022. Rainfall amounts between 1.00 and 2.00 inches were common. Periods of light to moderate rainfall began during the daytime hours on April 7 with the steadiest and heaviest rainfall arriving during the evening hours on April 7 into the overnight hours on April 8 before ending.||This heavy rainfall led to a retaining wall to partially collapse along Williams Street in Brattleboro, causing flooding.||In addition to the heavy rainfall, strong winds developed across Bennington County with peak gusts in the 40-57 mph range.
episodes.168654: Low pressure tracked through the Northeast bringing periods of heavy rain to central New York, particularly the Upper Delaware river basin. This resulted in minor to moderate flooding of the headwater tributaries.
episodes.169462: A cold front moving through the area brought multiple rounds of rain on April 7th. The front approached and a low pressure system developed over the area resulting in moderate to heavy rain over Northeast New Jersey. 2 to 3 inches of rain fell over a several hour period. This resulted in river and poor drainage flooding.
episodes.169463: A cold front moving through the area brought multiple rounds of rain on April 7th. The front approached and a low pressure system developed over the area resulting in moderate to heavy rain over the Lower Hudson Valley in New York. 2 to 3 inches of rain fell over a several hour period. This resulted in river and poor drainage flooding.

events.narrative: Several roads were closed in the Town of Mohawk due to flooding.

Several roads throughout Montgomery County were closed due to flooding, some of which included the villages of Hagaman and Fultonville and the towns of Palatine, Canajoharie, Root, Charleston and Glen. Overall, the county experienced 21 road closures, 2 damaged road culverts, 2 mudslides, 1 foundational collapse of a home and 3 motor vehicle accidents.
Several roads within the cities of Gloversville and Johnstown were closed due to flooding along with some basement flooding.

Numerous roads were closed throughout Ulster County, some of which occurred in Marbletown, Kingston, Saugerties, Stone Ridge, Rosendale, Gardiner, Wawarsing and New Paltz. Basement flooding was also reported in Stone Ridge.
Garber Square and West Ridgewood Ave Area, Streets closed due to flooding.
Paramus PD report Route 17 Northbound as flooded.

Flooding occurred in multiple areas within Schoharie County including Seward, Richmondville, Cobleskill, Breakabeen and Gilboa, causing roads to close. Heavy rainfall led to a mudslide on Flat Creek Road near Gilboa.
Basement water issues reported on Sunset Ave and on Heights Road.
Paramus PD report Route 17 Northbound near Linwood Ave is flooded.
A small landslide occurred near the Batcheller Creek and South Shore Road near the Town of Edinburg due to flooding.
Car submerged in flood water on South Pascack Road.
Right lane of Route 208 Northbound near Morlot Ave closed due to flooding. Left Lane partially passable.

The Saddle River at Lodi rose above its minor flood stage of 5.5 feet at 9:15pm EDT. It then continued to rise, surpassing major flood stage (8.0 feet) at 2:45 am EDT on April 8th before cresting at a height of 8.99 feet at 7:00am EDT. The river then gradually receded, eventually falling below minor flood stage at 1:00pm EDT on April 8th.
Residence filling with water on Route 59.
Nine feet of water and rising in basement on Hickory Street.
Route 7 Eastbound at the Interchange of I-787 had the left lane closed due to flooding near Green Island.
Several roads were closed due to flooding within the Town of Coxsackie in addition to some flooding of basements.
Flooding of the Mayfield Creek caused damage to a bridge along Riceville Road in the Village of Mayfield.
South Shore Road between Fayville Road and Northville Road was closed near the Town of Providence due to a landslide.
Water Rescue of occupant in vehicle stuck in flood waters on Grotke Rd.
Route 59 east and westbound all lanes closed due to flooding between Rt 303 and Palisades Center Drive.
Flooding conditions reported at Pearl River High School.

Several incidents of flooding occurred within Warren County, including the areas of Thurman, Warrensburg, Chestertown, Weavertown and Lake George. Road closures and possible washouts were reported within the towns of Warrensburg and Thurman. In Lake George, severe damage occurred to a driveway and parking lot of the Lakeview Terrace Hotel and Fairview Association.

U.S. Route 4 between North Wrights Loop and South Wrights Loop was closed in the Town of Stillwater due to flooding. In addition, a small bridge was compromised on Lohnes Road near Phillips Road in Stillwater.
Several roads were closed within the areas of Clifton Park, Malta, Ballston, Ballston Spa, Ballston Lake and Saratoga Lake due to flooding.
The westbound lane of Route 5 at Johnson Road was closed due to flooding in Rotterdam Junction.
Flooding was reported along Miller Road near Route 9W in Selkirk. Flooding was also reported along Marshall Road near Route 143 near Ravena.

Several roads were closed due to flooding across Cairo, Leeds, Jefferson Heights and Catskill. One water rescue was performed in Catskill as a person was trapped in their car which was surrounded by floodwaters.
A section of Pennsylvania Avenue in Palenville was closed due to flooding.
The southbound lane of U.S. Routes 9 and 20 were closed at Elliot Avenue due to flooding.
Route 9G was cut off when water cascading off Mount Merino collided with flooding from the swollen Hudson River at high tide.
A few road closures were reported in Pawling, Lagrangeville, Fairview and Poughkeepsie due to flooding. Some of the roads in Pawling suffered minor washouts.

The Ramapo River at Mahwah rose above its minor flood stage of 8 feet at 11:30pm EDT. It then continued to rise before cresting at a height of 8.31 feet at 4:30am EDT on April 8th. The river then gradually receded, eventually falling below minor flood stage at 2:45pm EDT on April 8th.
Brattleboro Department of Public Works imposed travel restrictions along Williams Street in Brattleboro due to damage from a retaining wall causing water to flow over the roadway.

Heavy rainfall led to excessive runoff into the East Branch Delaware River below the Pepacton Reservoir. The stream gage located near Harvard, NY reached a crest of 12.76 feet on April 8th at 2:30 PM. This is considered to be moderate flooding. Several roads were closed in the area of the stream gage, including NY SR 30.
In Fairhaven, lightning struck a home on Main Street, near Woodcock Way. The strike resulted in a fire on the gas line in the basement.
In New Bedford, two cars were stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Purchase Street and Deane Street at the railroad underpass.
In Acushnet, a car was stuck in two feet of street flooding on Middle Road.
In New Bedford, a car was stuck in flood waters on Belleville Avenue.

The Mohawk River at the Freeman's Bridge at Schenectady went over its banks and led to minor flooding in the area. This included at Riverside Park where part of the parking lot and playground were covered in water.
Heavy rain brought flooding to the Ouachita River at Thatcher Lock and Dam in early April.
